title: Constructible-quotient extensions descend to a finite stage of the kernel
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\ell$ be prime and $R$ a commutative Noetherian $\mathbf F_\ell$-algebra. Work in sheaves of $R_X$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A sheaf is constructible if its inverse-image restrictions to the members of some finite locally closed stratification are locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module values [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(H_a)_{a\in I}$ be subobjects of a module sheaf $H$, with $H_a\subseteq H_b$ for $a\leq b$ and $\varinjlim_a H_a\simeq H$ under the inclusion maps [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $G$ be constructible. For every short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]
$$0\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow0,$$
there exist $a\in I$, a short exact sequence $0\to H_a\to F_a\to G\to0$, and a morphism of this sequence to the given sequence whose maps on the ends are the inclusion $H_a\to H$ and the identity of $G$. The induced map $F_a\to F$ is a monomorphism, and the square formed by $H_a\to F_a$ and $H\to F$ is a pushout in module sheaves, meaning that maps from $F$ to any module sheaf are exactly compatible pairs of maps from $F_a$ and $H$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 7.4.4, printed p.306 (PDF p.312), the finite-stage realization of the extension class in Ext^1(G,H). This is the global extension-class assertion, not sheaf-valued internal Ext.

from.place: Proof, Step 1 of lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve: 'Relative Verdier duality, biduality ... over the same arbitrary field $k$', through lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality, lem-per-finite-residue-dualizing and lem-per-potential-local-duality; the last node's Step 2 extends finite-field coefficients.; coefficient comparison via ILO XVII 7.6.1, proof p. 314. Subargument: ILO XVII 7.6.10 closed/open devissage. Dependency of the localization-devissage argument: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.6.3, Proposition 7.6.5, Corollary 7.6.6 and Proposition 7.6.7, pp. 311-313; arbitrary Lambda-algebra coefficients in the application in Lemma 7.6.10. Corollary 7.6.6 concerns the closed immersion i (the word ouverte in its printed statement is a typo, as the complementary-open proof shows). Supporting the finite-simple-object devissage in ILO XVII 7.6.5: directed-partition and coefficient tensor devissage of XVII 7.4.2-7.4.6. Finite-stage descent of the extension class in the proof of ILO XVII Lemma 7.4.4, used to pass from one stratum to a directed partition.
